mainTopic: Does רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule (that a lost object found where many people pass becomes the finder's because the owner gave up hope) apply only where most people are גוים, or also where most are Jews? Includes רב אסי's ruling on a found barrel of wine.
overview: The גמרא keeps asking whether רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule applies only where most people are גוים, or also where most are Jews. His rule is that a find in a busy place belongs to the finder because the owner gave up hope. A proof from רב אסי's ruling on a found wine barrel is pushed away: רב אסי may agree with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר in one case and disagree in the other. רב אשי explains that רב אסי's 'permitted as a find' refers to the jug, since the wine itself is forbidden. Then comes a series of stories. In one, coins in נהר בירן must be announced. In another, שמואל says a purse found in the market belongs to the finder but should be returned לפנים משורת הדין, while רב נחמן lets the finder keep it. A third case is meat snatched by a kite. Each story is checked against רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule and explained as a special case. Last, a slaughtered goat found between טבריא and ציפורי leads to רבא's idea of two majorities: the population was mostly non-Jewish, but the slaughterers were mostly Jews. A new משנה then begins listing found items that must be announced.

steps.title: Another way out: the earlier source can follow the Rabbis
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another answer to the earlier proof. The source can follow the רבנן, because it never says the find belongs to the finder. It only says he does not have to announce it. He sets it aside, and a Jew who gives an identifying sign takes it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: really, this follows the רבנן. Does the source say 'they are his'? It says 'he is not obligated to announce.' He should set the item aside, and if a Jew comes and gives an identifying sign, he takes it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to reject the earlier proof that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule applies only where most people are גוים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier proof assumed that the source lets the finder keep the item, which only רבי שמעון בן אלעזר would allow. Now the גמרא reads the source more carefully: it only frees the finder from announcing. That fits the רבנן too, because the item still goes back to a Jewish owner who comes with a סימן.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces another possible answer
Really, actually: keeping the original assumption
To announce publicly that an item was found
An identifying sign that proves ownership

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not obligated to announce' is not the same as 'he may keep it.' This whole answer depends on keeping those two ideas apart.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
actually, it follows the Rabbis.
Does it teach "they are his"?
It teaches "he is not obligated to announce."
So he should set it aside, and a Jew will come
and give an identifying sign in it, and take it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְעוֹלָם רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second rejection of the proof from the earlier source, which came before this section.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the earlier source must follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the source lets the finder keep the item. It only frees him from announcing.

steps.title: רב אסי's ruling on a found barrel of wine
steps.stepSummary: A new proof is brought. רב אסי rules that someone who finds a wine barrel in a mostly-gentile city may keep it as a find, but may not benefit from the wine. If a Jew gives an identifying sign, the finder may drink it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear what רב אסי said: if someone finds a barrel of wine in a city where most people are גוים, it is permitted to him as a find, but the wine is forbidden for benefit. If a Jew comes and gives a sign in it, the finder may drink it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רב אסי's ruling. This sets up a new proof about where רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule applies, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wine is presumed to belong to a גוי, so it is forbidden as gentile wine, but the find itself may be kept. Once a Jew gives a סימן, the wine is known to be Jewish and may be drunk. Even so, the finder keeps it and does not return it to the Jew who gave the sign.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: introduces a source used as proof
Permitted to keep as a lost-and-found item
Forbidden to get any benefit from

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rav Asi said:
If one found a barrel of wine
in a city whose majority is gentiles,
it is permitted as a found item,
and forbidden for benefit.
phrases.notes: The wine is assumed to be a גוי's wine, and that kind of wine is forbidden.

phrases.english: If a Jew came and gave an identifying sign in it,
it is permitted for drinking, to its finder.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the last proof was pushed away, a new source is brought to answer the same question.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule applies only where most people are גוים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב אסי's ruling on a wine barrel found in a mostly-gentile city.

steps.title: The proof: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר speaks only of a gentile majority
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי's ruling must follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, since the finder keeps the barrel even after a Jew gives a sign. Because רב אסי speaks of a mostly-gentile city, the גמרא concludes that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule applies only there, and not where most people are Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's. Learn from this that when רבי שמעון בן אלעזר spoke, he meant a place where most people are גוים, but not a place where most people are Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the proof from רב אסי. His ruling follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, so רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule must be limited to a gentile majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the רבנן, the barrel would go back to the Jew who gave a סימן. Since רב אסי lets the finder keep it, he must hold like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר that the owner gave up hope. Since רב אסי mentions only a mostly-gentile city, the גמרא takes that as the limit of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? Whose opinion does this follow?
Learn from this: draws a conclusion
A place where most people are gentiles

phrases.english: Like whom? Like Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.
Learn from this

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר –
phrases.english: that when Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said his rule,
it was where most are gentiles,
but where most are Jews, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן? כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר. שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from רב אסי's ruling quoted in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule is limited to a place where most people are גוים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב אסי, who follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר and speaks only of a mostly-gentile city.

steps.title: רב אסי may agree in one case and disagree in the other
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר may hold his rule even where most people are Jews. רב אסי could agree with him about a gentile majority and disagree with him about a Jewish majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, I can tell you that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said his rule even where most people are Jews. רב אסי agrees with him in one case and disagrees with him in the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from רב אסי by showing that his ruling does not tell us how far רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's own rule goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that רב אסי holds exactly like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר in every way. The גמרא says no: רב אסי may follow him only in a gentile-majority city. So רב אסי's limit is his own, not רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, I can tell you: introduces a rejection

steps.whatToRemember: A later אמורא can follow a תנא in one case and disagree in another. So an אמורא's ruling does not prove how far the תנא's own view goes.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rejection does not settle whether רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule is limited to a gentile majority. The גמרא keeps testing it through the stories in steps 10, 20 and 28.

phrases.english: Really, I can tell you
that Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar
said his rule even where most are Jews,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב אַסִּי סָבַר לַהּ כְּווֹתֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא,
phrases.english: and Rav Asi holds like him in one case,
phrases.notes: This is the mostly-gentile city, the case רב אסי talked about.

phrases.english: and disagrees with him in one case.
phrases.notes: This is a place where most people are Jews.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אֲפִילּוּ בְּרוֹב יִשְׂרָאֵל נָמֵי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the conclusion drawn in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule is limited to a gentile majority.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed רב אסי follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר in every case, when he may agree only partly.

steps.title: What does 'permitted as a find' mean if the wine is forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about רב אסי's wording. If the wine is forbidden for benefit, what is the point of saying the barrel is permitted as a find?
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the wine is forbidden for benefit, what practical law does 'permitted as a find' teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to רב אסי's ruling and asks what the phrase 'permitted as a find' is there for. This sets up רב אשי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Permission to keep a find seems useless if you cannot get any benefit from it. So the גמרא wants to know what the finder actually gains.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, once it is so that
For what practical law? What difference does it make?

phrases.english: But since it is forbidden for benefit,
this 'permitted as a find'
for what practical law is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דַּאֲסִירָא בַּהֲנָאָה מוּתֶּרֶת מִשּׁוּם מְצִיאָה, לְמַאי הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the wording of רב אסי's ruling from step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the finder gains from 'permitted as a find' when the wine itself is forbidden.

steps.title: רב אשי: it refers to the jug
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that 'permitted as a find' refers to the barrel itself. The finder may keep and use the container, even though the wine is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: it is for its jug.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question: the finder may keep the container.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the wine falls under the ban on gentile wine. The jug itself is a found object the finder may use. That is what 'permitted as a find' gives him.
steps.whatToRemember: In רב אסי's case the wine is forbidden, but the finder may keep the container.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: for its jug.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: לְקַנְקַנָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Permitted as a find' lets the finder keep and use the container.

steps.title: Coins found in the Biran River
steps.stepSummary: A man found coins tied in a cloth in נהר בירן, and רב יהודה told him to announce them.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man found four coins tied up in a cloth that had been thrown into נהר בירן. He asked רב יהודה, who told him: go announce it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a man who found coins in a river, and רב יהודה ruled that he must announce the find. This story sets up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Announcing means the finder cannot keep the coins yet; he must try to find the owner. That is surprising for two reasons the גמרא will raise: the coins were in water, and the area was mostly gentile.

keyTerms.meaning: The Biran River, a river in Bavel

phrases.english: There was a certain man who found
four coins that were tied up in a cloth
and thrown into the Biran River.
He came before Rav Yehuda.
He said to him: Go announce it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּאַשְׁכַּח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new incident after the discussion of רב אסי's wine barrel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Coins found in נהר בירן must be announced.

steps.title: Isn't this like something swept away by the sea?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: an item lost in water should count as זוטו של ים and belong to the finder.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't this like the tide of the sea?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה's ruling. Something swept away by water is normally given up by its owner, so why must the finder announce it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: With זוטו של ים, the owner gives up hope (יאוש) because he assumes the water carried the item away for good. If these coins were in the same situation, the finder could keep them, and announcing would be pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: The tide of the sea; an item swept away by water, which the owner gives up on

phrases.english: But isn't it the tide of the sea!
phrases.notes: This points to the rule that whatever the sea sweeps away belongs to the finder, because the owner gives up hope.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא זוֹטוֹ שֶׁל יָם הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יהודה's ruling in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's ruling that the coins must be announced
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An item lost in water is זוטו של ים, the owner has given up, so the finder should keep it.

steps.title: The Biran River has obstacles
steps.stepSummary: נהר בירן is different: things get caught in it, so the owner does not give up hope.
steps.simpleTranslation: נהר בירן is different. Since it has obstacles, the owner does not give up hope.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this particular river is not like the open sea. Items get stuck in it, so the owner still expects to get his coins back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of זוטו של ים depends on the owner giving up. In נהר בירן things get caught and can be recovered, so there is no יאוש, and the finder has to announce.

keyTerms.meaning: It has obstacles; things get caught in it
He does not give up hope

phrases.english: The Biran River is different,
since it has obstacles, the owner does not give up hope.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי נְהַר בֵּירָן, כֵּיוָן דְּמִתְּקִיל לָא מִיָּאַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any item lost in water is זוטו של ים and belongs to the finder.
steps.terutzMaskana: נהר בירן catches items, so the owner does not give up, and the find must be announced.

steps.title: Does this disprove רבי שמעון בן אלעזר?
steps.stepSummary: The area was mostly gentile, so requiring an announcement seems to show the הלכה is not like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But most people there are gentiles! Conclude that the הלכה is not like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, even where most people are gentiles!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second challenge. Because the area was mostly gentile, רב יהודה's ruling seems to go against רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says that where most people are gentiles, the finder keeps the item. Since רב יהודה ordered an announcement in a mostly gentile area, it seems he rejects רבי שמעון בן אלעזר completely.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; conclude from it

phrases.english: But the majority there are gentiles,
conclude from this that the halacha is not
like Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar
even where there is a majority of gentiles!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רוּבָּא גּוֹיִם נִינְהוּ, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge on the same story, now about the gentile majority.
steps.kashyaTarget: Whether רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule is accepted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In a gentile-majority area רבי שמעון בן אלעזר lets the finder keep the item, but רב יהודה required announcing.

steps.title: Jews built and maintain the river
steps.stepSummary: Jews dammed נהר בירן and Jews dredge it, so the coins likely belong to a Jew who has not given up.
steps.simpleTranslation: נהר בירן is different, because Jews dammed it and Jews dredge it. Since Jews dammed it, assume the coins fell from a Jew. Since Jews dredge it, the owner does not give up hope.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this river is a special case, so the story says nothing about the general rule. The people working on the river are Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives two reasons. Since Jews work at the dam, the owner is probably Jewish, even though the town is mostly gentile. And since Jews clean out the river, he expects the coins to turn up, so he has not given up. The ruling against keeping the coins comes from these special facts, not from rejecting רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

phrases.english: The Biran River is different,
because Jews dammed it
and Jews dredge it.
Since Jews dammed it,
say that it fell from a Jew,
and since Jews dredge it,
the owner does not give up hope.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי נְהַר בֵּירָן, דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל סָכְרוּ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case by its special facts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה rejects רבי שמעון בן אלעזר even in a gentile majority.
steps.terutzMaskana: At נהר בירן the owner is likely a Jew who has not given up, so the general rule does not apply.
steps.whatToRemember: The נהר בירן story proves nothing against זוטו של ים or רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. The river is a special case: items get caught in it, and the Jews who work on it are likely owners who have not given up.

steps.title: שמואל's rulings on a purse found in the market
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that a purse found in the market belongs to the finder, but must be returned if a Jew gives a סימן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה was walking behind שמואל in the grain market. He asked: if someone found a purse here, what is the law? שמואל said: it belongs to him. And if a Jew came and gave a סימן? שמואל said: he must return it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story. רב יהודה asks שמואל two questions about a purse found in the market, and שמואל gives two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer lets the finder keep the purse. The second answer requires him to return it once a Jew proves it is his. The next step points out that these two answers seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: He is obligated to return it

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda was walking along
behind Mar Shmuel
in the market where pounded grain was sold.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מָצָא כָּאן אַרְנָקִי, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: He said to him: If one found a purse here, what is the law?
He said to him: These belong to him.

phrases.aramaic: בָּא יִשְׂרָאֵל וְנָתַן בָּהּ סִימָן, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: If a Jew came and gave an identifying sign for it, what is the law?
He said to him: He is obligated to return it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה הֲוָה שָׁקֵיל וְאָזֵיל בָּתְרֵיהּ דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new incident on the same subject of finding items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A purse found in the market belongs to the finder, but if a Jew gives a סימן he must return it.

steps.title: Two answers that contradict
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה objects that שמואל's two answers contradict each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two contradictory things!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה challenges שמואל. If the purse already belongs to the finder, how can he be obligated to give it back?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once an item legally belongs to the finder, the original owner's סימן should make no difference. Saying both 'it is his' and 'he must return it' looks like a contradiction.

phrases.english: Two contradictory rulings!
phrases.notes: Literally just 'two.' He means these two answers can't both be true.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's two answers in step 12.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the purse belongs to the finder, he cannot also be obligated to return it.

steps.title: Returning it is beyond the letter of the law
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that returning the purse is only לפנים משורת הדין.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: that is beyond the letter of the law.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל explains that his two answers work on different levels. Strict law lets the finder keep the purse, while returning it is a matter of going beyond the law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'These belong to him' is the strict law. 'He must return it' describes the right thing to do, which is more than the law demands. So the two answers do not contradict.

keyTerms.meaning: Beyond the letter of the law; doing more than the law requires

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not changing his first answer. By strict law the purse still belongs to the finder; returning it is extra goodness, not a legal requirement.

phrases.english: He said to him: That is beyond the letter of the law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לִפְנִים מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two levels: strict law versus going beyond it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both answers are strict law, so they contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: By law the finder keeps the purse; returning it is לפנים משורת הדין.

steps.title: שמואל's father returned donkeys
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's father returned donkeys he found in the desert even after a full year, going beyond the letter of the law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the time שמואל's father found donkeys in the desert and returned them to their owner after twelve months, beyond the letter of the law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports שמואל's idea with a story about his father. He returned lost donkeys long after he could legally have kept them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The donkeys were found in the desert and returned only after a whole year. He did not have to return them, but he did so לפנים משורת הדין. This is the same kind of extra goodness שמואל described for the purse.
steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, a purse found in the market belongs to the finder by law. Returning it to a Jew who gives a סימן is לפנים משורת הדין, like his father's conduct with the donkeys.

phrases.english: Like that case where Shmuel's father
found those donkeys in the desert
and returned them to their owner
after twelve months of the year,
beyond the letter of the law.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דַּאֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the idea of לפנים משורת הדין from step 14.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's idea that returning such an item is beyond the law
steps.raayaSupportSource: The conduct of שמואל's father with the donkeys

steps.title: רב נחמן's rulings on the same purse
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that the finder keeps the purse even if a Jew gives a סימן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא was walking behind רב נחמן in the tanners' market, and some say in the market of the Sages. He asked: if someone found a purse here, what is the law? רב נחמן said: it belongs to him. And if a Jew came and gave a סימן? He said: it still belongs to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a similar story in which רבא asks רב נחמן the same two questions. This time both answers are 'it belongs to the finder.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike שמואל, רב נחמן does not mention returning the purse even after a סימן is given. The next step challenges this.

phrases.english: Rava was walking along
behind Rav Nachman
in the tanners' market,
and some say in the market of the Sages.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מָצָא כָּאן אַרְנָקִי, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: He said to him: If one found a purse here, what is the law?
He said to him: These belong to him.

phrases.aramaic: בָּא יִשְׂרָאֵל וְנָתַן בָּהּ סִימָן, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: If a Jew came and gave an identifying sign for it, what is the law?
He said to him: These belong to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא הֲוָה שָׁקֵיל וְאָזֵיל בָּתְרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story to step 12 with a different answer to the second question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The finder keeps the purse even after a Jew gives a סימן.

steps.title: But the owner is crying out
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects: the owner is standing there and protesting that it is his.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he is standing and screaming!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב נחמן. How can the finder keep the purse when the owner is right there, proving it is his and demanding it back?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner's protest seems to show that he never gave up on the purse. If so, the finder should not be allowed to keep it.

phrases.english: But isn't he standing and screaming!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא עוֹמֵד וְצוֹוֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's second answer in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that the finder keeps the purse after a סימן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The owner's protest shows he still wants it, so it should go back to him.

steps.title: Like screaming over a sunken ship
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the owner's protest is useless, like crying over a collapsed house or a sunken ship.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is like someone screaming over his house that fell down or his ship that sank in the sea.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers that the owner's cries do not change anything. The purse is already gone from him, just like a fallen house or a sunken ship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Crying out after the loss does not undo the fact that the owner already gave up on the purse. Once the purse belonged to the finder, the owner's protest has no legal power.
steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן holds that once the purse belongs to the finder, the owner's סימן and protests do not take it back. His cries are like mourning a sunken ship.

phrases.english: He becomes like one screaming over his house that collapsed
or over his ship that sank in the sea.

steps.triggerLanguage: נַעֲשָׂה כְּצוֹוֵחַ עַל בֵּיתוֹ שֶׁנָּפַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison to a loss that cannot be undone
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The owner's protest proves he still owns the purse.
steps.terutzMaskana: Protest after the loss is meaningless; the finder keeps the purse.

steps.title: Meat dropped by a kite
steps.stepSummary: A kite grabbed meat in the market and dropped it in a grove. אביי told the finder to keep it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A kite grabbed meat in the market and dropped it among the palm trees of בר מריון's house. The finder came to אביי, who told him: go take it for yourself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story about meat that a bird carried off and dropped. אביי ruled that the finder may keep it, and the questions that follow are about this ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי treats the meat as ownerless, which lets the finder keep it. The גמרא will now ask whether this goes too far and whether the meat is even allowed to be eaten.

phrases.english: There was a certain kite that took meat in the marketplace
and threw it among the palm trees of the house of Bar Maryon.
He came before Abaye,
phrases.notes: "He" is the man who found the meat under the trees.

phrases.english: He said to him: Go take it for yourself.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דַּיּוֹ דְּשָׁקֵיל בִּשְׂרָא בְּשׁוּקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new incident about a found item.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meat dropped by a kite may be kept by the finder.

steps.title: Does this follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר even among Jews?
steps.stepSummary: The meat market was mostly Jewish, so letting the finder keep the meat seems to follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר even in a Jewish majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: But most people there are Jews! Conclude that the הלכה is like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר even where most people are Jews!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's ruling. Since the market was mostly Jewish, letting the finder keep the meat seems to stretch רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule into a Jewish majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of step 10. There, a ruling seemed to reject רבי שמעון בן אלעזר even in a gentile majority. Here, a ruling seems to apply his rule even in a Jewish majority, which goes back to the question from steps 3 and 4.

phrases.english: But the majority there are Jews,
conclude from this that the halacha is
like Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar
even where there is a majority of Jews!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רוּבָּא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל נִינְהוּ, שָׁמְעַתְּ מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's ruling in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's ruling and the reach of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Letting the finder keep meat from a Jewish market implies רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule applies even in a Jewish majority.

steps.title: A kite is like the tide of the sea
steps.stepSummary: Meat taken by a kite is like זוטו של ים, so the owner gives up hope no matter who he is.
steps.simpleTranslation: A kite is different, since it is like the tide of the sea.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the finder keeps the meat for a different reason. Once a bird has snatched it, the owner gives up, just as he would if the sea swept it away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling does not depend on רבי שמעון בן אלעזר or on who lives there. Meat carried off by a bird is treated like זוטו של ים, which belongs to the finder even among Jews.

phrases.english: A kite is different,
since it is like the tide of the sea.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי דַּיּוֹ, דִּכְזוֹטוֹ שֶׁל יָם דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר even in a Jewish majority.
steps.terutzMaskana: Meat taken by a kite is like זוטו של ים, so the finder keeps it regardless of the majority.

steps.title: Isn't meat that left sight forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges using רב's rule that בשר שנתעלם מן העין is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב said: meat that was hidden from sight is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem. Even if the finder may own the meat, how can he eat it when רב forbids meat that was out of sight?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This challenge is not about ownership. It is about whether the meat is kosher to eat. Meat that went unwatched might have been swapped for non-kosher meat, so רב forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat that was hidden from sight (left unwatched)

phrases.english: But didn't Rav say:
Meat that was hidden from sight is forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר רַב: בָּשָׂר שֶׁנִּתְעַלֵּם מִן הָעַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate challenge to אביי's ruling, about eating rather than owning the meat.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's permission to take and use the meat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The meat left sight while the bird carried it, so by רב's rule it should be forbidden.

steps.title: He watched it the whole time
steps.stepSummary: The case is where the finder stood and watched the meat the whole way.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he stands and sees it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the finder kept his eyes on the meat from the moment the bird took it until it landed. So it never left sight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's rule applies only when no one saw the meat for a while. Here it was watched the whole time, so it is not בשר שנתעלם מן העין, and אביי's ruling stands.
steps.whatToRemember: Meat snatched by a bird is like זוטו של ים, so the finder may keep it even in a Jewish area. It is permitted to eat only if the finder watched it the whole time, so it never became בשר שנתעלם מן העין.

phrases.english: This is where he stands and sees it.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעוֹמֵד וְרוֹאֵהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The meat was out of sight and is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The finder watched it the whole time, so רב's rule does not apply.

steps.title: רבי חנינא finds a slaughtered goat on the road
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא found a slaughtered young goat between טבריא and ציפורי, and the חכמים allowed him to have it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא found a slaughtered young goat between טבריא and ציפורי, and they permitted it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story about a found slaughtered animal. The חכמים allowed the finder to have it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two questions are hidden in this short story. First, may the finder keep someone else's lost item? Second, may he eat meat when he does not know who slaughtered it? The next step will separate these two questions.

keyTerms.meaning: Tiberias, a city in the Galil
Tzippori, another city in the Galil

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina found a slaughtered young goat
between Tiberias and Tzippori
and they permitted it to him.
phrases.notes: The text does not say who; it means the חכמים.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא מָצָא גְּדִי שָׁחוּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story of the kite and the meat, the גמרא brings another story about found meat.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slaughtered goat found on the road between טבריא and ציפורי was permitted to the finder.

steps.title: Two separate reasons for the permission
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי explains that the finder could keep it because of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, and could eat it because of רבי חנניא בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: They permitted it to him as a lost item following רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. They permitted it as a kosher slaughter following רבי חנניא, the son of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי explains the story by splitting the permission into two parts: keeping the find, and eating the meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For keeping the find, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר allows a finder to keep an item when the owner has given up hope, as with items found among a majority of non-Jews. For eating the meat, he relies on רבי חנניא, who trusts that slaughtered animals found this way were properly slaughtered. Each part depends on a different תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: Regarding the laws of finding lost items
Regarding the laws of kosher slaughter
The תנא who holds that the owner gives up hope in certain cases, so the finder may keep the item

keyTerms.term: רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who permits eating found slaughtered animals

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two questions. Being allowed to keep the goat does not by itself mean you may eat it; each needs its own reason.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
They permitted it to him regarding finding
according to Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar,
and regarding slaughter

phrases.aramaic: כְּרַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי.
phrases.english: according to Rabbi Chananya son of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי הִתִּירוּהוּ לוֹ מִשּׁוּם מְצִיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the permission in the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The permission to keep the find follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר; the permission to eat it follows רבי חנניא בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי.

steps.title: The ברייתא where רבי חנניא permits found slaughtered animals
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה forbids lost animals found slaughtered, while רבי חנניא permits them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: If someone lost his young goats and roosters, then went and found them slaughtered, רבי יהודה forbids them and רבי חנניא, the son of רבי יוסי הגלילי, permits them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רבי חנניא's opinion that רבי אמי relied on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner lost his animals and found them slaughtered, but he does not know who slaughtered them. רבי יהודה worries it was not done properly and forbids the meat. רבי חנניא permits it, and that is the view used for רבי חנינא's goat.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: As it is taught:
One whose young goats and roosters were lost,
went and found them slaughtered,
Rabbi Yehuda forbids,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי מַתִּיר.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Chananya son of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili permits.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא הֲרֵי שֶׁאָבְדוּ לוֹ גְּדָיָיו וְתַרְנְגוֹלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the second half of רבי אמי's explanation.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a תנא, רבי חנניא, who permits eating found slaughtered animals.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording a מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and רבי חנניא בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי.

steps.title: רבי splits the cases: garbage heap or house
steps.stepSummary: רבי says רבי יהודה is right when the animals were found in a garbage heap, and רבי חנניא is right when they were found in a house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: רבי יהודה's words seem right when he found them in a garbage heap, and רבי חנניא's words seem right when he found them in the house.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא) explains that the two תנאים may not really argue. Each one is talking about a different place where the animals were found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal thrown on a garbage heap was probably thrown out because its slaughter was not kosher, so it is forbidden. An animal found in a house was likely slaughtered properly, so it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה הנשיא, compiler of the משנה

phrases.english: Rebbi said:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה הנשיא, not רבי יהודה from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: The words of Rabbi Yehuda seem right
when he found them in a garbage heap,

phrases.aramaic: וְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
phrases.english: and the words of Rabbi Chananya son of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili
when he found them in the house.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with רבי's way of settling the מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtered animals found in a garbage heap are forbidden; those found in a house are permitted.

steps.title: If the meat is kosher, the area must be mostly Jewish
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that trusting the slaughter means most people there were Jews. Then keeping the find would follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר even in a Jewish majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since they permitted it to him regarding slaughter, the majority there must be Jews. Learn from this that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר even where most people are Jews!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from רבי אמי's explanation. If the slaughter was trusted, the area must be mostly Jewish, so letting the finder keep the goat would follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר even in a Jewish majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat is only trusted as kosher if it probably came from a Jew, which means a Jewish majority. But רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule about the owner giving up hope works where most people are non-Jews. So the story would mean his rule applies even among a Jewish majority, which is a big new claim.

phrases.english: Since they permitted it to him regarding slaughter,
the majority there are Jews,
learn from this
the law follows Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar
even where most are Jews!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּהִתִּירוּהוּ לוֹ מִשּׁוּם שְׁחִיטָה רוּבָּא יִשְׂרָאֵל נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אמי's two-part explanation.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's claim that keeping the find follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר while eating it follows רבי חנניא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Trusting the שחיטה requires a Jewish majority, which would stretch רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule to a Jewish majority.

steps.title: Mostly non-Jews, but mostly Jewish slaughterers
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that most of the people there were non-Jews, but most of the butchers were Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Most of the people were non-Jews, and most of the slaughterers were Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by showing that two different majorities were in play.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since most people were non-Jews, the owner gives up hope, so the finder may keep the goat under רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. Since most slaughterers were Jews, the meat is trusted as kosher. Nothing here requires רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule to apply in a Jewish majority.

keyTerms.meaning: Most of the butchers are Jews

steps.whatToRemember: One place can have two separate majorities: who lives there, which decides whether you may keep the find, and who slaughters there, which decides whether you may eat it.

phrases.english: Rava said:
A majority of non-Jews, and a majority of Jewish butchers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא רוֹב גּוֹיִם וְרוֹב טַבָּחֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case by splitting it into two separate majorities.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Trusting the שחיטה means the whole area was mostly Jewish.
steps.terutzMaskana: The population was mostly non-Jewish, so the find may be kept. The slaughterers were mostly Jewish, so the meat is kosher.

steps.title: רבי אמי finds slaughtered young birds
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי found slaughtered young birds between טבריא and ציפורי and was told to take them for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי found slaughtered young birds between טבריא and ציפורי. He came before רבי אסי; some say before רבי יוחנן, and some say to the בית מדרש. They told him: Go, take them for yourself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a similar story on the same road, and again the finder may keep what he found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same place as רבי חנינא's goat, so the same reasoning fits. The finder may keep the birds, and they are fit to eat. The story also records different versions of whom רבי אמי asked.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami found slaughtered young birds
between Tiberias and Tzippori,
he came before Rabbi Asi,
and some say before Rabbi Yochanan,
and some say to the study hall.
And they said to him: Go take it for yourself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַמֵּי אַשְׁכַּח פַּרְגִּיּוֹת שְׁחוּטוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another story on the same road with the same result.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtered birds found between טבריא and ציפורי may be kept by the finder.

steps.title: רבי יצחק נפחא finds a skein of net thread
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק נפחא found a skein of thread used for weaving nets and was told to take it for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק נפחא found a skein of thread from which nets are woven. He came before רבי יוחנן; some say to the בית מדרש. They told him: Go, take it for yourself.
steps.whatsHappening: A final short story: another finder asks, and again he is told he may keep the item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the item is not meat, so only the question of keeping it matters. The answer is the same: the owner has given up hope, so the finder may take it.

keyTerms.meaning: A skein, a bundle of thread
רבי יצחק the smith, an אמורא

steps.whatToRemember: In the stories of the birds and the skein of thread, as with רבי חנינא's goat, the finder was told he may keep the item. Not every story on this amud ends that way: in the נהר בירן case רב יהודה required an announcement.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha found
a skein from which nets are woven,
he came before Rabbi Yochanan,
and some say to the study hall,
and they said to him: Go take it for yourself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא אַשְׁכַּח קִיבּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: One more story of a finder told to keep his find, closing the series.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A found skein of net thread may be kept by the finder.

steps.title: New משנה: found items that must be announced
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins listing found items that the finder must announce, such as produce in a vessel, coins in a pouch, and piles of produce or coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: And these items one must announce: if he found produce in a vessel, or a vessel by itself; coins in a pouch, or a pouch by itself; piles of produce, piles of coins.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. Earlier the list was items the finder may keep; now it lists items he must announce. The list continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These items have a sign that can identify the owner: the container itself, or the way the items are piled. So the owner has not given up hope, and the finder must announce what he found.
steps.confusionAlert: This משנה is the opposite list from the earlier one. Before, the items were the finder's to keep; here, the finder must announce them.

phrases.english: MISHNA
And these one is obligated to announce:
if he found produce in a vessel,
or a vessel by itself.
Coins in a pouch,
or a pouch by itself.
Piles of produce, piles of coins,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵלּוּ חַיָּיב לְהַכְרִיז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the stories about items the finder may keep.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Found items with an identifying container or arrangement, such as produce in a vessel, coins in a pouch, or piles, must be announced.
